question: Where does the PRODUCT lose each stroke end-to-end (not per-subsystem)?
method: lab:cascade — per gold target event, read the shipped per-case report artifacts and evaluate explicit stage criteria: TARGET (product tap/seed path, coverage ≥0.5) → EVENT (≥50% overlap or gold contact inside selection) → PADDLE (tracked, coverage ≥0.3) → BALL (tracked) → CONTACT (|err| ≤ 66ms) → PHASE (segmented, ordering valid) → STROKE (L1 side match). Conditional survival = product view.

results.verdict: 1/5 gold strokes complete the full chain (wm-volley-02). Every loss has a distinct named cause: dink → contact error 147ms (ball-body overlap region); rally1 → EVENT SELECTION picked a 0%-overlap window (paddle-speed proposal defect; poisons contact/phase/stroke: predicted FOREHAND vs gold BACKHAND_VOLLEY); rally2 → ball untracked (BALL_BODY_OVERLAP) though contact still landed 62ms via paddle-only; vic (held-out) → phase followEnd ≤ contact (known v2 inversion defect).

modelingNotes: Stage order forces BALL before CONTACT; rally2 shows contact can succeed without ball (paddle-anchored) — the conditional column understates that path. Recorded, not hidden.
EVENT overlap for passing cases is 30-65% — selections are systematically NARROWER than gold events (proposal bounds tight around the peak). Contact-inside saves them today.
n=5: the waterfall SHAPE is the diagnosis; the rates are not stable estimates.
highestLeverage: EVENT selection decoupling from paddle-speed peaks (rally1's 0%-overlap selection is exactly the known merge-cascade defect measured from a new direction)
PHASE v2 ordering guard (one-line invariant fix candidate: reject/repair followEnd ≤ contact) unlocks the held-out case
BALL body-overlap remains the ball blocker (known, exhibits exist)
